grh_ee9038d1218a898c6510.title: Homecoming
paragraphs: Sailor Enoch Arden leaves his wife Annie and their children for a long voyage meant to secure the family's future, but a wreck strands him far from home for years. Annie waits until hope is almost gone, then eventually marries their devoted friend Philip. When Enoch finally returns, he sees Annie happy with Philip and their new child and chooses not to destroy that peace. Dying in obscurity, he reveals himself to Miriam and asks that Annie be told only after his death, but Annie reaches him in time for a final farewell and his blessing on her new life.

Lee as radio adaptor, Gordon MacRae as host, and Marvin Miller as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 29 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.a80b23d73cb026ed|The Association Of American Railroads (middle commercial deleted)]].

grh_ee3e888e332260ecc886.title: The Joke's on Guess Who
paragraphs: Decorated war veteran Will Hinchcliff arranges a fake alley mugging so he can disarm the supposed attacker and prove his courage to his wife Judy. The practical joke collapses into real violence, leaving Judy and the man hired to play the mugger dead. As police and friends try to make sense of the disaster, Will's guilt exposes a deeper motive: he has never reconciled surviving the war while so many of his friends died, and happiness has felt like something he did not deserve. What was meant to make him look heroic instead destroys the life he was trying to prove worthy of.

[[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Barney Phillips, Robert Towers, Peggy Webber, Shepard Menken, and Joan McCall. grh_ee264c42e2a2ae3e2d3f.title: Xx War Bond Special
paragraphs: A War Bond special reprises dramatized passages from Ernie Pyle's Here's Your War about American infantrymen in North Africa. Pyle describes exhausted soldiers carrying heavy weapons after days of combat, their longing for home, their kindness toward local children and the emotional changes produced by prolonged fighting. The program ends among the graves of men left behind as units move to the next battlefield, using Pyle's account to urge listeners to support the surviving soldiers through the purchase of war bonds.
